newsitem.title: UK: WORLD BONDS - Short end BTPs best bet after rate cut.
newsitem.headline: WORLD BONDS - Short end BTPs best bet after rate cut.

text.p: Italian BTPs are vulnerable to a bout of profit-taking near term after Friday's half point cut in official interest rates, economists said on Monday.
But canny investors should use any sell-off to pile into the two-year sector, as short-end convergence trades and expectations of further rate cuts join forces to push that part of the curve higher.
"Over the very near term, I'd look for the spread to give something back on profit-taking," said Ros Lifton, senior international economist at HSBC Markets here.
"But the front end of the curve should continue to do reasonably well."
The Bank of Italy took markets by surprise on Friday by shaving 50 basis points from its discount rate to 6.25 percent, the lowest level for almost 22 years.
It also trimmed 50 basis points from its fixed term advances, or Lombard rate, to 7.75 percent.
While the cut was expected, the timing was not, after tough comments from Bank of Italy governor Antonio Fazio last month.
Bt 1110 GMT, the 10-year BTP/Bund spread was at 116 basis points, off its record 111 basis points reached last week. The two-year spread was at 255 basis points.

Phyllis Reed, European bond strategist at BZW, said the biggest scope for convergence trades in BTPs was very much at the front end, on enforced convergence in official interest rates as European monetary union (EMU) approaches.
"The long end of the market is getting to levels that look a bit stretched -- the 10-year spread could go to 100 basis points in the next few months but that would be it for now," she said.
"You're much better off in the front end -- that's really where the value is.
Reed said investors holding longer Italian paper should start thinking about taking profits, particularly as the 10-year spread approaches 100 basis points.
"It's a good idea to take profits and move down the yield curve, put on steepening trades and by doing that you're shorting duration too which is not a bad thing at the moment," said Reed.

Brian Venables, senior bond analyst at ABN AMRO in Amsterdam, expected the 10-year BTP/Bund spread to narrow to around 50 to 60 basis points in the next year as more interest rate cuts come through. But he said it would be a slow grind.
"We definitely won't get another move on rates for at least another month, probably not until after the budget is sorted out," he said.
The government must present its 1998 budget to parliament by September 1997.
Italy has trailed other European countries in trimming official rates, even though Friday's cut was the fourth in the last 12 months.
Venables said he expected the Bank of Italy to slice another 150 basis points off official interest rates, but added it was in no rush.
Analysts said of all the peripherals, Italy probably offered the greatest value at the moment as both economics and politics were working in the same direction.
"Italy makes an interesting case compared with the other peripherals," said Lifton.
She said Spain and Portugal would also see some convergence in their short rates next year, but added they did not need it so much from an economic perspective.
"So some of the others have only the political impetus but not really the economic justification (for rates to come down)," she said.
